A test worth running on your own service catalogue.

Name a benefit whose eligibility turns only on age. The state knows every citizen's date of birth exactly. If that benefit still requires an application, the barrier is not data — and it is falling hardest on the people least able to clear it.
A note on the word “predictive.”
Proactive services are often described as predicting when a citizen will need something. In practice, every working example triggers on a
fact that has been registered
— a birth recorded, an income filed — not on a forecast of future need. Detect events; do not forecast needs.

sections.title: The assistant arrives, and the question is whose.

runs.text: What changes · 04
The assistant arrives, and the question is whose.

On current trajectory, a large and growing share of citizens in digitally mature states will reach government through a conversational agent within this period. The strategic question is not whether that happens. It is
whose agent it is
, and most governments are answering it by default rather than by decision. There are four options, and they are not exclusive:

blocks.caption: The assistant arrives, and the question is whose.

runs.text: Option
What it means
When it applies
Build
A first-party government assistant
Where the state has the capability to run it; necessary anyway for authenticated transactions
Publish
A machine-reachable service surface any authorised agent can call
Almost always — and it is what makes the first-party assistant work too
Partner
Deliver inside a private platform with population reach
Where reach cannot be achieved otherwise, accepting dependency
Regulate
Conditions on assistants that mediate public services — accuracy disclosure, liability, no unauthorised transactions
Necessary regardless of the other three; we have not found a government that has
The missing infrastructure for all four is
delegation

: proving that a named person authorised a named agent to take a named action, with a scope, an expiry and a revocation. Versions for human intermediaries work at scale in several countries. We have not found a national digital identity that lets a citizen authorise a software agent to act, with a scope, an expiry and a revocation.

It is worth building for a reason beyond agents. A carer acting for an elderly parent, an accountant acting for a business, an advice worker acting for a claimant and an AI agent acting for a citizen all need the same thing: scope-limited, time-bounded, revocable, auditable authority to act on someone else's behalf.
The assisted-access problem and the agentic-government problem are one problem.
Solving it serves the most digitally excluded citizens and the most technically advanced use case with the same infrastructure — which is also the version that survives a political conversation.

sections.title: Language is an engineering constraint, not a translation task.

runs.text: What changes · 05
Language is an engineering constraint, not a translation task.
Türkiye has real benchmarks, and they produce two findings that should change how a model is chosen.

blocks.caption: Language is an engineering constraint, not a translation task.

runs.text: Measured
GPT-4o
Claude 3.5 Sonnet
Llama 3.3
Gemini 1.5 Pro
Gemma2-27B
TR-MMLU: 6,200 questions across 62 categories, 39 models evaluated. TurkishMMLU, built on 10,000+ natively written questions, independently places the same model at the top.
Measured Turkish performance is what counts.

The Cetvel benchmark compares Turkish-centric and multilingual models on Turkish tasks and finds large differences between them. Model selection for a Turkish-language service should be made on measured Turkish performance.
And one question to settle early.

e-Devlet operates Turkish-first with an English toggle, and some documents are issued in additional languages. Where a service answers in more than one language, which version governs an automated determination is worth settling in policy before the first determination.
Tokenisation is a cost line and an accuracy driver.

Turkish runs at roughly 2.19 to 2.84 tokens per word across major tokenisers. The share of valid Turkish tokens correlates with benchmark score at r = 0.90 — the same property drives both the bill and the quality.
A sovereign model is in development.
BİLGE, from TÜBİTAK BİLGEM, spans 1B to 122B parameters trained on a trillion words, intended for government services. It belongs on the same benchmarks as every other candidate.
And the plan reaches beyond Turkish.
The 2026–2030 plan commits to a joint Turkic-languages model with the Organization of Turkic States, across the Oghuz, Kipchak and Karluk branches.

sections.title: The rules that will shape this, and where they come from.

runs.text: What changes · 06
The rules that will shape this, and where they come from.
Türkiye's AI law is before the Assembly, and the EU's already reaches Turkish organisations.
In Türkiye
KVKK.

Law 6698 binds public institutions, with VERBİS registration for public bodies from April 2019. Law 7499 (in force 1 June 2024) added adequacy decisions, binding corporate rules and standard contractual clauses to the transfer regime.
Localisation.
Sectoral data localisation is dense — banking, payments, capital markets, health, telecoms and tax, plus Circular 2019/12 for critical public data. In-country inference is the legal default.
AI law.

Three bills are before the Assembly; the 2024 proposal is shaped on the EU AI Act and is in committee. The AI Action Plan commits to five sectoral regulatory sandboxes and an ethics board within a year.
And the European timetable

As an EU candidate country and a major exporter, Türkiye is doubly exposed to the EU AI Act: it binds Turkish organisations whose system output is used in the Union, and it is the template the pending domestic bill follows. These dates are the practical planning horizon.

blocks.caption: The rules that will shape this, and where they come from.

runs.text: Date
What
Detail
Transparency
A person must be told they are interacting with an AI system, from the start of the first interaction. Article 50 — already in force, and not deferred.
High-risk duties
Full obligations where AI is used to determine eligibility for essential public services: impact assessment, human oversight, logging, registration. Annex III, point 5.
No grandfathering for public bodies
Legacy AI already in use by a public authority must comply. Private-sector legacy systems are exempt absent significant change. Public ones are not. Article 111(2).

These are the dates in the EU AI Act — Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 — as amended by the Digital Omnibus, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, published in the Official Journal on 24 July 2026. The high-risk duties were deferred by roughly sixteen months. They were not weakened.

sections.title: Two tracks, always running. Neither waits for the other.

runs.text: How to start
Two tracks, always running. Neither waits for the other.
No government can stop shipping for three years while it fixes its registers. It does not have to, and the evidence says it should not try.

blocks.caption: Two tracks, always running. Neither waits for the other.

runs.text: Track one · the service track
Track two · the foundation track
Visibility
Visible
Invisible
Tempo
Weeks to months
Quarters to years
Content
Services shipped into the foundation you already have. Requirements removed. Journeys consolidated. Conversational entry added in front of what works.
Registers corrected. Rules turned into code. Services exposed as callable functions. Delegation and assurance built.
What it buys
The credibility and the budget for the other track
What the first track will be able to ship next year
The foundation does not decide whether you ship. It decides which services you can ship into — and each quarter of foundation work opens the next tier.
So the sequencing question becomes a portfolio question
Ship now
— services whose facts already sit in a register you trust. Renewals, confirmations, status, pre-filled returns.
Ship next
— services needing one register corrected or one rule written as code. Scope the foundation work from the service you want, not the other way round.
Ship later
— services needing cross-entity integration or a legal change. Start that work now; do not hold the first two tiers behind it.
How Türkiye has actually done it
Türkiye shows that foundations-first works. A register is a precondition; the AI Action Plan is the programme that can now build on it.
Register first, channel second — and now a deliberate scan-pilot-scale model.
This is not a theory — it is the observable operating model.
Türkiye is the clean counter-example — and that is the advantage.

The identifier was universal in 2000 and the register live in 2002, six years before the gateway opened. Foundations genuinely came first. That is not an argument against running both tracks: it is the reason Türkiye can now run the service track at full speed, because the foundation others are still building is already paid for.
Growth was incremental by design.
Institutions onboard one at a time by protocol, inheriting shared authentication and payments. There was no big-bang migration and no second platform.
The AI plan is explicitly staged.
Scan, then pilot, then scale: 30+ pilots across 10+ ministries in twelve months in at least two waves, with a scale gate at six to twelve months.
With named ownership in every institution.
An AI manager per institution, a three-year roadmap within twelve weeks of appointment, and mandatory AI literacy training with micro-certification across the public workforce.

sections.title: Six priorities. Not six phases.

runs.text: Priorities
Six priorities. Not six phases.
Not six phases. Each produces something you can hold at the end of it.

blocks.caption: Six priorities. Not six phases.

runs.text: Priority
What it produces
Remove the requirement before automating it
A list of requirements for one service line, each with an owner and a date by which it is either justified or gone.
Make the registers right for the services you are shipping into
A one-page readiness note per candidate service: what the register covers, how current it is, and whether it records the fact at the resolution the decision needs.
Turn one service's rules into code
The eligibility logic of one high-volume service, running in parallel with the existing process and tested against cases already decided — including appeals that were upheld.
Retire the legacy that blocks the next tier
A list of the systems standing between you and the services you want next, with funded dates.
Stand up assurance before the first incident
A register of automated decisions — not of systems — with a named owner for each.
Publish performance, including who it does not reach
One page per service per quarter: completion, first-time-right, abandonment and exclusion by group, appeals and overturns.
Nothing here says “deploy a model.”

That is deliberate. The model is the least scarce input in this programme and the easiest to change. Governments that start by procuring a model and work backwards to the service consistently end up with an assistant in front of an unchanged process.

sections.title: Three of the four real benefits are not cost reduction.

runs.text: Impact and benefits
Three of the four real benefits are not cost reduction.
What the evidence supports, and how much of it applies here.
Take-up
Proactive delivery closes the gap between who is entitled and who claims. This is the largest single citizen benefit available, and
it increases expenditure
Consistency
Rules as code remove variation between offices and officials, and make the effect of a policy change immediate and testable rather than a year of retraining.
Compressed variance
The best causal evidence available — a field study of 5,172 customer-support agents given a generative AI assistant (Brynjolfsson, Li and Raymond,
Generative AI at Work

, Quarterly Journal of Economics, 2025), a private-sector setting that must be treated as an analogue — shows AI raising output by about a third for the newest and least skilled workers, with little effect for the most experienced. In benefits assessment, casework and first-line advice, where governments face high turnover and long ramp times,
the value is bringing new staff to competence faster, not making the best caseworkers better.
Speed
Application-to-decision latency disappears where the state already holds the facts. Processing measured in hours has fallen to seconds in production proactive services.

Applicability in Türkiye: consistency and speed are the strongest fits, on an estate of 1,128 institutions, where one consistent standard applied across all of them is the largest single prize. Take-up applies directly — BSYS already demonstrates the mechanism, eliminating roughly 10% duplicate payments while reaching 30 million citizens.
Why time saved is not money saved

This is the gap that undermines most government AI business cases, and there is a plausible mechanism for it. Careful labour-market research — Humlum and Vestergaard's study of some 25,000 Danish workers in eleven exposed occupations (
Large Language Models, Small Labor Market Effects
, 2025) — finds self-reported time savings among users alongside
no measurable effect on earnings or hours
at the population level, while around one worker in twelve reported entirely new tasks created by the tools. The hypothesis, and it is a hypothesis rather than an established causal finding, is that
saved time is absorbed by verification, review and governance before it ever reaches a budget line.
It is testable. A government running an AI programme should measure the new work as deliberately as the saved work.
The business case to make, and the one to avoid
For conversational services, build the case on
first-time-right completion, error reduction and diverted contact-centre volume
— not on deflection, and not on headcount.

Proactive delivery increases outlay and reduces administrative cost. The outlay increase is the point. Any business case showing a large net saving is almost certainly counting money recovered from citizens.
For proactive services, state the arithmetic at the outset:

That is the earliest available warning of a programme heading for the failure mode described above — visible in the finance annex, before a line of code is written. The honest case is: this costs more, it reaches the people the law intended to reach, and it reduces the cost of serving the people it already reached.
The measurement problem

We could not locate a current government cost-per-transaction-by-channel dataset published anywhere since 2012, any published containment or resolution rate for a named government conversational service, or any controlled comparison of conversational service initiation against conventional forms.
A government that commissions its own baseline in the first quarter of an AI programme will be the only party in the room able to say whether it worked.
That is the cheapest high-value item on this entire list.
One metric to refuse to report:
containment or deflection
. It measures a citizen failing to reach a human, no audit institution publishes it, and it will be optimised at the expense of every other number.

sections.title: Start where the foundation already reaches.

runs.text: The position
Start where the foundation already reaches.

Then extend it, one tier at a time, while the service track keeps shipping. Bring one high-friction journey and the people accountable for it; leave with the requirements to remove, the register-readiness note, the register of automated decisions and the baseline nobody currently holds.
Discuss a service to redesign
This quarter
Service track
— Pick services whose facts already sit in a register you trust — renewals, confirmations, status, pre-filled returns. Remove the requirements you cannot justify. Ship.
Foundation track
— Scope the foundation work backwards from the services you want next year, not from an abstract maturity model.
Governance
— Write down one boundary before anything else: an offer the citizen confirms is safe; an adverse determination applied automatically on inferred data is not.

Candidate journeys in Türkiye: a workplace licence re-issue; a nüfus kayıt örneği issued from the register; a sosyal yardım application, where the 52 automated checks already exist and the decision boundary matters most.

sections.title: Most governments use AI. Almost none is AI-native.

runs.text: The distinction
Most governments use AI. Almost none is AI-native.
If you could remove the model and the service would still work as designed, the service is AI-enabled. If removing the model would make the service impossible, the service is AI-native.
Most governments now use AI. There are assistants on portals, transcription in meetings, summarisation in the back office, translation at the counter. This is AI
in
government. It leaves the service itself unchanged: the citizen still works out which service they need, still gathers the documents, still applies, still waits.

blocks.caption: Most governments use AI. Almost none is AI-native.

runs.text: Today
AI-native
Who starts
The citizen applies
The state offers and the citizen confirms
How they ask
Find the service, then the form
Say what they need, in their own words
Who does the legwork
The citizen collects and submits
The state does what it already can
What the rule is
Guidance a person interprets
Code that executes, tests and explains
What the person does
Assesses from scratch
Confirms or corrects — and is accountable
Who can act
The citizen, through a browser
The citizen, or an agent they authorised
By that test, very little in production anywhere is yet AI-native. That is not a criticism. It is the size of the opportunity.
What it is not
Not a chatbot on the portal.
Roughly two in five European government portals already offer automated live support. That is the previous generation, at scale.
Not a count of deployed use cases.
Inventories are growing quickly; most entries are pilots, internal productivity tools, or assistive features on unchanged services.
Not a claim any government can currently make in full.
The gap between the narrative and the volume is universal. A government that closes it honestly will be more credible than one that announces it.

sections.title: Six elements constitute it. Governance is one of six, not the whole.

runs.text: The six elements
Six elements constitute it. Governance is one of six, not the whole.

Intent replaces navigation · the state never asks twice · rules execute rather than only publish · the state takes the first step · every service is reachable by a machine · accountability attaches to each decision.
Intent replaces navigation
The citizen says what they need in ordinary words, and the state works out which service, rule and process applies.
Requires
a complete, current, machine-readable description of every service the government offers — which most governments do not yet have.
The state never asks twice
Anything the state already holds is never requested from the citizen again.
Requires
registers that are right at the granularity the decision needs, and a legal basis for internal data use.
Rules execute, not only publish
Entitlement exists as code that can be run against a case, re-tested when policy changes, and explained in ordinary language — not only as guidance a trained official interprets.
Requires
policy and engineering working as one function. That is an organisational change, not a technical one.
The state takes the first step
Where the facts are already known and the entitlement is clear, the state offers and the citizen confirms — rather than the citizen applying and the state assessing.
Requires
registers accurate at the right granularity and period, and an explicit rule that adverse determinations are always visible and disputable before they take effect.
Every service is reachable by a machine
Services are exposed as callable functions with defined inputs, outputs and authorisation — not only as pages a human clicks through.
Requires
a way to prove that a specific person authorised a specific agent to take a specific action, and to revoke it.
Accountability attaches to each decision
For any determination a machine contributed to, the government can say who is responsible, on what basis it was made, and how a citizen challenges it.

sections.title: The only bloc that has made interoperability a legal duty.

runs.text: Where the European Union stands
The only bloc that has made interoperability a legal duty.
Europe's distinctive asset is not any single platform. It is that the obligations run across twenty-seven administrations at once.
2018–2023 — The Single Digital Gateway.
Twenty-one key procedures fully digital and cross-border accessible by December 2023. The Once-Only Technical System went live on the same date.
2024 — Interoperable Europe Act.
Applies from 12 July 2024. Interoperability assessments mandatory from 12 January 2025 — attached to each delivery rather than gating a programme.
2024–2026 — The Digital Identity Wallet.

Regulation 2024/1183 obliges every Member State to provide at least one wallet within 24 months of the implementing acts — a deadline of 24 December 2026. As of September 2026, three Member States had a wallet in production — Italy at scale with over ten million activations, Denmark since June, Greece — Germany plans January 2027, and the deadline stands.
2026 — A settled AI rulebook.
Regulation 2026/1744 was published on 24 July 2026, confirming the timetable for high-risk obligations on public bodies.

sections.title: Conversation opens the service. A structured object completes it.

runs.text: What changes · 01
Conversation opens the service. A structured object completes it.
Conversational access will become normal. It will not replace transaction. The distinction is distributional and it decides where money is spent:
The head of the distribution
— renew, pay, check status, upload — is high volume, well understood by the citizen, and already well served by forms. A dialogue turn here adds time and cost and nothing else.
The tail
— ambiguous, cross-departmental, “which of these applies to me” — is where navigation has always failed and where conversation is transformative.

The business case is not conversation versus forms. It is conversation versus the phone call that a failed digital journey generates. Rank services by call volume relative to transaction volume and start at the top.

sections.title: What we mean by “the card”.

runs.text: What changes · 02
What we mean by “the card”.
A definition, because the term is used loosely and the distinction matters.

An action card is a structured, interactive component the service returns into the conversation: typed fields that carry their own validation, pre-filled with what the state already holds, an explicit statement of what the citizen is agreeing to, and one button that commits it.
Five bands, in order
Identity and context
Who this is for and what it concerns — resolved, not retyped.
Pre-filled, from the register
What the state already holds, shown so it can be corrected.
Deltas only, validated
Just what has changed. Each field carries its own rule and its own error message.
The consequence, computed
Fee, entitlement, date, outcome — shown before commitment, not after.
The declaration, then one action
What the citizen attests to, and a single committing button.
Not a bespoke build — the formats already exist
Adaptive Cards
Microsoft’s declarative JSON card format, rendered natively by the host. Input types are Text, Number, Date, Time, Toggle and ChoiceSet; actions are Submit, OpenUrl, ShowCard and Execute.
MCP Apps (SEP-1865)
Published 21 November 2025, authored by OpenAI and Anthropic maintainers with the MCP-UI creators. Templates are pre-declared so a host can review them before they run.
Messaging equivalents
WhatsApp Flows, RCS interactive messages and Apple Messages for Business all render multi-field forms inside the conversation. Governments already reach citizens on these channels.

Schema version 1.3 of Adaptive Cards added required-field marking, validation patterns, error messages and labels together — the standard itself concluded a card without them was not fit for purpose. WCAG 3.3.4 says the same thing in law-adjacent terms: for legal or financial submissions, the action must be reversible, checked, or confirmed — and the last two require a reviewable object the citizen can see.
And there is a government-specific reason the object matters.

The objection is that a transcript is a perfectly good record. It is — of what was said. But when a citizen later asks why a decision went the way it did, or simply wants to check what they agreed to, the useful record is what they were
shown

: which options were on the screen, which fields were validated, and what sat above the button they pressed. A transcript cannot reproduce that. A structured submission can, and the citizen can be shown it again at any point.
And one architectural rule follows:

the card is rendered by the trusted system, not written by the model. The model chooses which card and which fields; the registry fills them. This keeps personal data out of the prompt, stops a compromised model fabricating a convincing but false declaration, and keeps the record of what the citizen saw under the state's control. Privacy, security and legal control in one decision.
Three cards, field by field
Real procedures in the European Union, taken from Annex II of the Single Digital Gateway Regulation. The fields, the validation and the declaration are the point — figures are illustrative.

sections.title: The state takes the first step, for a definable class of service.

runs.text: What changes · 03
The state takes the first step, for a definable class of service.
The class is definable, and a government should define it explicitly before a programme starts rather than case by case during one. A service qualifies when all four are true:
A service qualifies when all four are true
The facts that determine entitlement are
already held
by the state, in an authoritative register.
Those facts are correct
at the granularity and for the period
the determination requires.
The determination is
an award
, not a liability or a reduction.
If it is wrong, the error is
visible and recoverable

An offer the citizen confirms is safe and lawful. An adverse determination applied automatically on inferred data is the failure mode behind the best-known failures in this field. That is a governance boundary, not a technical one — write it down before the programme starts.

A note on the word “predictive.”
Proactive services are often described as predicting when a citizen will need something. In practice, every working example triggers on a
fact that has been registered
— a birth recorded, an income filed — not on a forecast of future need. Detect events; do not forecast needs.

sections.title: The assistant arrives, and the question is whose.

runs.text: What changes · 04
The assistant arrives, and the question is whose.

On current trajectory, a large and growing share of citizens in digitally mature states will reach government through a conversational agent within this period. The strategic question is not whether that happens. It is
whose agent it is
, and most governments are answering it by default rather than by decision. There are four options, and they are not exclusive:

blocks.caption: The assistant arrives, and the question is whose.

runs.text: Option
What it means
When it applies
Build
A first-party government assistant
Where the state has the capability to run it; necessary anyway for authenticated transactions
Publish
A machine-reachable service surface any authorised agent can call
Almost always — and it is what makes the first-party assistant work too
Partner
Deliver inside a private platform with population reach
Where reach cannot be achieved otherwise, accepting dependency
Regulate
Conditions on assistants that mediate public services — accuracy disclosure, liability, no unauthorised transactions
Necessary regardless of the other three; we have not found a government that has
The missing infrastructure for all four is
delegation

: proving that a named person authorised a named agent to take a named action, with a scope, an expiry and a revocation. Versions for human intermediaries work at scale in several countries. We have not found a national digital identity that lets a citizen authorise a software agent to act, with a scope, an expiry and a revocation.

It is worth building for a reason beyond agents. A carer acting for an elderly parent, an accountant acting for a business, an advice worker acting for a claimant and an AI agent acting for a citizen all need the same thing: scope-limited, time-bounded, revocable, auditable authority to act on someone else's behalf.
The assisted-access problem and the agentic-government problem are one problem.
Solving it serves the most digitally excluded citizens and the most technically advanced use case with the same infrastructure — which is also the version that survives a political conversation.

sections.title: Language is an engineering constraint, not a translation task.

runs.text: What changes · 05
Language is an engineering constraint, not a translation task.
In EU law there is no privileged source text. That is a design constraint on automated determination, not a translation problem.

blocks.caption: Language is an engineering constraint, not a translation task.

runs.text: Measured
English
Greek
Slovenian
Bulgarian
Latvian
Lithuanian
Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct average across the EU20 benchmark suite, 21 languages. On MMLU the English-Lithuanian gap is 18 points; on HellaSwag the English-Latvian gap is 25.
The gap tracks training-data share, not language difficulty.

Performance correlates with each language's share of common crawled text — Lithuanian at 0.16%, Latvian at 0.12%, Slovenian at 0.15%. This is a supply problem with a known shape, which is why the Union is addressing it as infrastructure rather than as procurement.
And one question to settle early.

Because every language version is equally authentic, a determination generated in one language and served in another is not a translation of the decision — it is the decision. Evaluation has to cover every language a service is delivered in.
All language versions are equally authentic.
Regulation 1/1958 and Article 55(1) TEU; the Court in CILFIT requires comparison across language versions to interpret any provision. An automated determination has no fallback original.
The Union is building the supply side.
ALT-EDIC was established in February 2024 with an explicit public-administration mandate. EuroLLM covers all 24 official languages; OpenEuroLLM is funded under Digital Europe.
And the benchmark already exists.
The EU20 suite evaluates 40 models across 21 languages. A Member State can choose a model on measured performance in its own language today.

sections.title: The rules that will shape this, and where they come from.

runs.text: What changes · 06
The rules that will shape this, and where they come from.
Unusually for this field, a European public body can plan against a known timetable.
In the European Union
Deployer duties.

AI Act Article 26 requires human oversight by competent persons with authority to intervene, monitoring, incident reporting and log retention for at least six months. Article 26(8) adds a public-authority duty to verify EU database registration before use.
Impact assessment.

Article 27 requires a fundamental rights impact assessment from bodies governed by public law and private entities providing public services, notified to the market surveillance authority. The Omnibus now allows it to cross-reference the DPIA, and the AI Office is to supply a template.
Procurement.

The Commission's Model Contractual Clauses for AI exist in high-risk and light versions, translated into all 24 languages. They are an AI Act compliance overlay — the commercial terms still need drafting.
And the European timetable
These are the dates in Regulation 2024/1689 as amended by Regulation 2026/1744, published in the Official Journal on 24 July 2026. They apply directly, without national transposition.

blocks.caption: The rules that will shape this, and where they come from.

runs.text: Date
What
Detail
Transparency
A person must be told they are interacting with an AI system, from the start of the first interaction. Article 50 — already in force, and not deferred.
High-risk duties
Full obligations where AI is used to determine eligibility for essential public services: impact assessment, human oversight, logging, registration. Annex III, point 5.

Legacy AI already in use by a public authority must comply. Private-sector legacy systems are exempt absent significant change. Public ones are not. Article 111(2).

These are the dates in the EU AI Act — Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 — as amended by the Digital Omnibus, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, published in the Official Journal on 24 July 2026. The high-risk duties were deferred by roughly sixteen months. They were not weakened.

sections.title: Two tracks, always running. Neither waits for the other.

runs.text: How to start
Two tracks, always running. Neither waits for the other.
No government can stop shipping for three years while it fixes its registers. It does not have to, and the evidence says it should not try.

blocks.caption: Two tracks, always running. Neither waits for the other.

runs.text: Track one · the service track
Track two · the foundation track
Visibility
Visible
Invisible
Tempo
Weeks to months
Quarters to years
Content
Services shipped into the foundation you already have. Requirements removed. Journeys consolidated. Conversational entry added in front of what works.
Registers corrected. Rules turned into code. Services exposed as callable functions. Delegation and assurance built.
What it buys
The credibility and the budget for the other track
What the first track will be able to ship next year
The foundation does not decide whether you ship. It decides which services you can ship into — and each quarter of foundation work opens the next tier.
So the sequencing question becomes a portfolio question
Ship now
— services whose facts already sit in a register you trust. Renewals, confirmations, status, pre-filled returns.
Ship next
— services needing one register corrected or one rule written as code. Scope the foundation work from the service you want, not the other way round.
Ship later
— services needing cross-entity integration or a legal change. Start that work now; do not hold the first two tiers behind it.
How the European Union has actually done it
The Union's own instruments are the strongest evidence for parallel delivery: eIDAS 2 lands wallet issuance and public-sector acceptance on a single date, rather than sequencing one behind the other.
Parallel by law, with a short head start only where a mandate is involved.
This is not a theory — it is the observable operating model.
Estonia released foundation and service together.
X-Road and the national ID card came out in the same year, 2002, and services grew concurrently. Private-sector internet banking had already normalised digital credentials six years earlier.
Denmark is the one clean foundations-first case.

NemID in 2010, the Digital Post Act in 2012, mandatory for business in 2013 and citizens in 2014. The lead is three to four years — and it was the mandate that required the foundation, not the service.
The Union legislates the two tracks together.

The Single Digital Gateway set the same December 2023 deadline for the 21 procedures and for the once-only system. The Interoperable Europe Act attaches an assessment to each delivery rather than gating the programme.
But foundations do not produce proactive services on their own.
Seventeen years separated X-Road from Estonia's first proactive service. Proactive delivery has to be separately commissioned — it does not emerge from good plumbing.

sections.title: Six priorities. Not six phases.

runs.text: Priorities
Six priorities. Not six phases.
Not six phases. Each produces something you can hold at the end of it.

blocks.caption: Six priorities. Not six phases.

runs.text: Priority
What it produces
Remove the requirement before automating it
A list of requirements for one service line, each with an owner and a date by which it is either justified or gone.
Make the registers right for the services you are shipping into
A one-page readiness note per candidate service: what the register covers, how current it is, and whether it records the fact at the resolution the decision needs.
Turn one service's rules into code
The eligibility logic of one high-volume service, running in parallel with the existing process and tested against cases already decided — including appeals that were upheld.
Retire the legacy that blocks the next tier
A list of the systems standing between you and the services you want next, with funded dates.
Stand up assurance before the first incident
A register of automated decisions — not of systems — with a named owner for each.
Publish performance, including who it does not reach
One page per service per quarter: completion, first-time-right, abandonment and exclusion by group, appeals and overturns.
Nothing here says “deploy a model.”

That is deliberate. The model is the least scarce input in this programme and the easiest to change. Governments that start by procuring a model and work backwards to the service consistently end up with an assistant in front of an unchanged process.

sections.title: Three of the four real benefits are not cost reduction.

runs.text: Impact and benefits
Three of the four real benefits are not cost reduction.
What the evidence supports, and how much of it applies here.
Take-up
Proactive delivery closes the gap between who is entitled and who claims. This is the largest single citizen benefit available, and
it increases expenditure
Consistency
Rules as code remove variation between offices and officials, and make the effect of a policy change immediate and testable rather than a year of retraining.
Compressed variance
The best causal evidence available — a field study of 5,172 customer-support agents given a generative AI assistant (Brynjolfsson, Li and Raymond,
Generative AI at Work

, Quarterly Journal of Economics, 2025), a private-sector setting that must be treated as an analogue — shows AI raising output by about a third for the newest and least skilled workers, with little effect for the most experienced. In benefits assessment, casework and first-line advice, where governments face high turnover and long ramp times,
the value is bringing new staff to competence faster, not making the best caseworkers better.
Speed
Application-to-decision latency disappears where the state already holds the facts. Processing measured in hours has fallen to seconds in production proactive services.

Applicability in the Union: take-up is the strongest fit anywhere in this page — over €1 billion of allowances went unclaimed in the Netherlands in a single year, and Estonia found 97% of proactive-benefit recipients had previously had to apply. Consistency matters most in federal and regionalised states. All four benefits apply; the constraint is the twenty-four-language evaluation burden.
Why time saved is not money saved

This is the gap that undermines most government AI business cases, and there is a plausible mechanism for it. Careful labour-market research — Humlum and Vestergaard's study of some 25,000 Danish workers in eleven exposed occupations (
Large Language Models, Small Labor Market Effects
, 2025) — finds self-reported time savings among users alongside
no measurable effect on earnings or hours
at the population level, while around one worker in twelve reported entirely new tasks created by the tools. The hypothesis, and it is a hypothesis rather than an established causal finding, is that
saved time is absorbed by verification, review and governance before it ever reaches a budget line.
It is testable. A government running an AI programme should measure the new work as deliberately as the saved work.
The business case to make, and the one to avoid
For conversational services, build the case on
first-time-right completion, error reduction and diverted contact-centre volume
— not on deflection, and not on headcount.

Proactive delivery increases outlay and reduces administrative cost. The outlay increase is the point. Any business case showing a large net saving is almost certainly counting money recovered from citizens.
For proactive services, state the arithmetic at the outset:

That is the earliest available warning of a programme heading for the failure mode described above — visible in the finance annex, before a line of code is written. The honest case is: this costs more, it reaches the people the law intended to reach, and it reduces the cost of serving the people it already reached.
The measurement problem

We could not locate a current government cost-per-transaction-by-channel dataset published anywhere since 2012, any published containment or resolution rate for a named government conversational service, or any controlled comparison of conversational service initiation against conventional forms.
A government that commissions its own baseline in the first quarter of an AI programme will be the only party in the room able to say whether it worked.
That is the cheapest high-value item on this entire list.
One metric to refuse to report:
containment or deflection
. It measures a citizen failing to reach a human, no audit institution publishes it, and it will be optimised at the expense of every other number.

sections.title: Start where the foundation already reaches.

runs.text: The position
Start where the foundation already reaches.

Then extend it, one tier at a time, while the service track keeps shipping. Bring one high-friction journey and the people accountable for it; leave with the requirements to remove, the register-readiness note, the register of automated decisions and the baseline nobody currently holds.
Discuss a service to redesign
This quarter
Service track
— Pick services whose facts already sit in a register you trust — renewals, confirmations, status, pre-filled returns. Remove the requirements you cannot justify. Ship.
Foundation track
— Scope the foundation work backwards from the services you want next year, not from an abstract maturity model.
Governance
— Write down one boundary before anything else: an offer the citizen confirms is safe; an adverse determination applied automatically on inferred data is not.

Candidate journeys in the Union: an Annex II procedure not yet completed end-to-end cross-border; a birth-triggered family benefit where the register already holds the facts; a pension claim where contribution periods can be retrieved rather than declared.
